NARROW FINDING RESOLVED at 13675fd0070ef5efb0b6bdb901f33922d27a6484

I independently checked the exact corrected observer blob 473d28772dafef86dc6f1ad6ea71496c6874d1a4 and test blob 5cce82a0091c43dbf30e5a66dce3e419361d773d. The finite network-code allowlist and fixed capture categories address both synthetic channels. All five original/current startup regressions pass on Node22.22.2 with zero failures/cancellations/skips in a minimal credential-free child environment; exact source hashes were preserved before/after. Original action results/errors, request status/timing, listener retirement and bounded hung capture remain covered. No candidate CLI/browser/profile or real credential was used.

This resolves only the new request/capture metadata finding. It does not qualify unchanged outer failure/page-error strings, all newly added historical/native evidence, physical devices, current production or all merge gates. Fresh exact-head CI and remaining source/preservation/publication safeguards are still required; do not reuse the prior head's green checks. The root implementation-design question is moot for this author-provided correction and must not become an artificial gate.

Root evidence: pr1565-review-13675fd0/root-verification.json and root-startup-tests.tap.

--- Original source-bound finding and reproduction history (preserved) ---

Exact-head startup-observer privacy contract gap at af4cd146f4ed05c79a404642978ae682e3486757 (scripts/smoke-fpv-public-fresh-install.mjs blob c920b42628d6d223b299ab7a68fda626bf406811).

I returned this PR to draft while this is resolved, to prevent automated merging from racing a new review finding. This does not change source, checks, budgets, branch history or the input-recovery runtime fix.

The new observer normalizes request.url() to pathname, but copies request.failure().errorText into report.requests[].failure (line 156), and copies state-capture error.message into captureFailure (line 187). A password-specific redact callback is not a general URL sanitizer.

A bounded VM probe of ONLY the exact exported observer, with invented strings and no CLI/import execution or real credential/browser-state access, demonstrated that failure text containing https://user:synthetic-userinfo@example.test/start.mjs?token=synthetic-query-secret#synthetic-fragment retains all three synthetic sensitive URL components in the report. The request resource itself correctly becomes /start.mjs. This proves the advertised no-query/no-credential report contract is not enforced for arbitrary failure strings; it does NOT establish that actual Chromium supplied such a string or that any real secret leaked.

Please add a regression covering URL/userinfo/query/fragment data in failure and capture-error strings, and retain only bounded known network/error categories or equivalently fail-closed sanitized metadata. Preserve the original startup failure/result, request status/timing and capture bound. Do not weaken application access controls or omit the failing startup.

Root evidence retained externally: pr1565-startup-metadata-boundary-probe.json and probe-pr1565-startup-metadata-boundary.mjs. Existing 740/740 practice and 10/10 pointer results remain accurately recorded; observer suite has 170 passes and one explicitly skipped historical pinned-snapshot case. Fresh exact-source gates and review are required after a fix.

Update 2026-10-17 14:56 UTC — Separate capture-error probe against the same exact source also retains synthetic URL userinfo/query/fragment in captureFailure. The original successful action result is preserved, event listeners are retired, and source SHA-256 2177e895551c37191df2113896cd9540438071cfcfeb42577b9f3fb948aa567c is unchanged. This remains an isolated synthetic contract test, not an observed real-browser leak. Evidence: pr1565-capture-error-boundary-probe.json; please cover both free-form fields in the corrective regression.
